gates.question: Which leak-scan shapes in a commit message leave the commit out of kbgit.py contribute?
options: the registry's private names and secrets only, the commit named by hash alone
every leak-scan shape with the project's allowlist, the trailer address added to it
gates.recommendation: the registry's private names and secrets only, the commit named by hash alone
gates.answer: the registry's private names and secrets only, the commit named by hash alone

notes: SP-qinvdomv review gap 2: kbcommon.leak_hits(message) with no allowlist flags the attribution trailer's email (116 of the last 200 commits carry it), so contribute leaves those commits out. BG-hia2m3hg's worker proposed the private-names-and-secrets scope; its gate was classed secrets, which the unattended run may not answer, so the sprint kept every leak-scan shape (the conservative choice) and this story carries the operator's choice. Plan 2026-10-20 (SP-rrqlgiff): operator gate g1 (class secrets) answered by the operator: the registry's private names and secrets only, the commit named by hash alone. Premise run on origin/main 8aa620db0 with the check's planted clone: contribute leaves out the trailer commit for an email hit (kg_contrib.py:180, kbcommon.leak_hits of the whole message), so no branch is made. The check was fixed at plan: it read the branch with check=True and crashed when no branch was made; it now treats a missing branch as no subjects and plants a third message with a fake secret built at run time. The guard narrows, so no planted refusal case is added to a test (no contribute test exists).
